newsitem.title: USA: Household International to buy Transamerica unit.
newsitem.headline: Household International to buy Transamerica unit.

text.p: Household International Inc. said Wednesday it has a definitive agreement to purchase Transamerica Corp.'s consumer finance business for $1.1 billion in cash.

With the agreement, Household said it will make significant progress toward expanding the HFC consumer finance branch network, the oldest in the country. The network provides consumer lending and credit card products in the United States, Canada and Britain.
Household is one of the nation's largest issuers of private-label and general purpose credit cards, such as the GM Card and the AFL-CIO's Union Privilege card.
The acquired branches will operate under the HFC brand.
The deal will boost Household's portfolio of core real estate-secured receivables by $3 billion, or almost 38 percent, and will bring its total managed assets to over $50 billion.
The purchase excludes delinquent receivables, it added.
"This acquisition brings us a very high-quality portfolio of real estate-secured loans, a great branch network, and many talented employees," said William Aldinger, chairman of Household.
Household said it expects the purchase to increase earnings this fiscal year, and that economies of scale will result in significant cost savings, which it did not specify.
Household, based in Prospect Heights, Ill., said it will finance the deal with a combination of debt and new common equity.

Transamerica, which provides specialised financial and life insurance products and services worldwide, said it will use proceeds from the sale to pay down debt and buy back up to 6 million common shares.
Transamerica said it would record its gain on the sale when the deal closes, prior to June 30, subject to regulatory approvals.
It said any gain would take into account taxes, writedowns of intangibles and the result of the continuing liquidation or sale of the remaining $280 million of special assets.
Transamerica, based in San Francisco, said the consumer finance business had a book equity of $487 million as of March 31.
Transamerica's stock rose $2.75 to $90 early on the New York Stock Exchange. Household rose $1 to $92.875, also on the NYSE.
